It also has validation concept (for node color) so it is pretty tailored for the protoarray it doesn't have the concept of justification\finalization yet. But it shows the data for the nodes Perfect, thanks I'm working on something similar but then I'll just focus on a different part and rely on your tool. It takes a JSON with those fields? We just removed the forkchoice dump endpoint cause it was a good time for a breaking change and it was borked due to having different forkchoice implementations. I will reinsert it only for the tree structure, not the protoarray one. But the dump should be a strict superset of the information you have there. with the caveat that I don't have the checkpoints, just the epochs. I already have a user request: I would draw the weights in a different way: I'd draw larger the descendant of the heaviest chain: so that when observing a branch I can quickly identify the canonical and first/second contending branch Yes, json I was thinking about better identify canonical chain. I'll check it. If you share your dump json I can make it load and start being multi client Share also your endpoint path

excerpts.author: tbenr
excerpts.content:
It should be a big problem to make it compatible with other data format. If clients could share their protodump file here I can make it work for them.
btw it is here: https://github.com/tbenr/protovis
the code is very messy and unclean. just a result of copy\paste here and there 🙂

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: is it dependant on protoarray in a deep way?

excerpts.author: tbenr
excerpts.content: it has the concepts of node slot (and epoch, for the background grid), weight (for dot sizes) and executionblock hash (for pandas and merge point). It also has validation concept (for node color)

excerpts.author: tbenr
excerpts.content: so it is pretty tailored for the protoarray

excerpts.author: tbenr
excerpts.content: it doesn't have the concept of justification\finalization yet. But it shows the data for the nodes

excerpts.content: Perfect, thanks I'm working on something similar but then I'll just focus on a different part and rely on your tool. It takes a JSON with those fields?
